text: . Benchmark domestic equity indices witnessed a sharp decline and were trading around 1.3% lower during the afternoon session. The Sensex tumbled 956 points to 72,939, while the Nifty shed 306 points to 22,835 when reports last came in.In the broader market at the National Stock Exchange, the Midcap 100 index fell 1.4%, while the Smallcap 100 index slid 1.6% a short while ago. On the sectoral front, all sectors were trading in the red, as a broad-based sell-off was seen across the board.

. Indian Navy will host second edition of commanders’ conference 2026 in New Delhi from today. Ministry of Defence said that the three day conference will provide an avenue for senior naval leadership, including outstation Operational and Area Commanders. It will undertake a comprehensive review of operational preparedness at the military-strategic level and engage with senior government functionaries through an institutionalised mechanism.The Ministry said that the conference will be pivotal in underscoring Indian Navy’s contribution towards safeguarding India’s maritime interests, including Security of Energy amidst the ongoing conflicts in West Asia. On the Opening Day of the conference, Defence Minister Rajnath Singh will share his vision and guidance on national maritime perspectives and expectations from Indian Navy. The Chief of the Defence Staff and the Chief of the Army Staff will also engage with Naval Commanders to foster tri-Services synergy and integration.

. FICCI FRAMES 2026 will begin in Mumbai today. The theme of this year’s FICCI FRAMES is “India’s Media Moment: Creating Value in an Age of Infinite Content.”Union Minister for Tourism and Culture Gajendra Singh Shekhawat will deliver the inaugural address of the FICCI FRAMES 2026. FICCI FRAMES Ambassador and actor Ayushmann Khurrana will also address the gathering. The inaugural session will also feature the FICCI FRAMES Lifetime Achievement Award, which will be presented to former FICCI President and JioStar Vice-Chairman Uday Shankar.The programme will include discussions on India’s screen economy, cinema, digital creators, sports viewing, artificial intelligence and copyright, among other issues.

. Union Agriculture and Farmers’ Welfare Minister Shivraj Singh Chouhan has called upon states to complete preparations for the Rabi season through coordinated planning, scientific assessment and close field-level monitoring. Addressing the two-day National Agriculture Conference – Rabi Campaign 2026 in New Delhi, Mr Chouhan said that amid climate change, erratic rainfall and water constraints, food security and higher farm incomes would require data-driven planning and stronger Centre-State coordination rather than conventional approaches.Expressing concern over drought conditions in Maharashtra and Karnataka, Mr Chouhan said nearly two-thirds of Maharashtra has been affected and the State has declared drought, while Karnataka is also facing drought-like conditions. He said a Central team will undertake a ground assessment in Karnataka on the 3rd of next month, while a Central team would also be sent to Maharashtra.The Minister assured that the Central Government stands firmly with farmers during the difficult situation. He also said that Maharashtra, Karnataka, Telangana and Andhra Pradesh would need crop plans based on water availability and soil moisture. Separate strategies should be prepared for rainfed and irrigated areas.Mr Chouhan urged states to promote pulses and oilseeds, particularly in areas that remain fallow after paddy cultivation. He also emphasised the balanced use of fertilizers, noting that excessive application raises cultivation costs and can affect soil health. He also suggested weekly monitoring in every state of crop conditions, sowing progress, germination, pest and disease attacks and market prices. He said real-time information would enable authorities to identify emerging problems and take corrective action without delay.

. At least six civilians have been killed and 53 others wounded in Russian attacks across several Ukrainian cities as fighting continues on the front lines. Ukrainian officials said three people were killed and eight wounded in the Kyiv region, while another three people were killed in a drone strike on an office building in Dnipro. In Kharkiv, a strike on a residential building wounded 38 people, including 10 children.Meanwhile, Ukraine has continued long-range drone attacks on targets inside Russia. Russian authorities said their air defences shot down 254 Ukrainian drones overnight, while fires were reported at three infrastructure facilities in the Krasnodar region.The attacks come after a week of diplomatic efforts at the United Nations aimed at advancing negotiations to end Russia-Ukraine war.In the latest battlefield developments, Ukraine’s Third Army Corps said its forces had recaptured another 51 square kilometres of territory in the Donetsk region, bringing the total area it claims to have retaken to 176 square kilometres since launching its recent offensive.Meanwhile, Russia’s Defence Ministry said its forces had captured two villages – Novovodiane in Donetsk and Ulanove in the Sumy region.The latest escalation comes as prospects for a quick diplomatic breakthrough remain uncertain.

. In Jammu and Kashmir, the Legislative Assembly today passed a resolution seeking the immediate restoration of full statehood to the Union Territory. The resolution was moved by Chief Minister Omar Abdullah and was passed by voice vote after a debate in the House.BJP legislators opposed the resolution and staged a walkout before the vote. The resolution calls for its forwarding to the Government of India for necessary action.

. Benchmark domestic equity indices ended on a positive note today. The Sensex rose 315 points to close at 73,896. The Nifty gained 77 points to settle at 23,141. The broader market at the National Stock Exchangedisplayed mixedtrend. The Midcap 100 index dropped over 0.1 per cent, while the Smallcap 100 index rose more than 0.1 per cent.In the forex market, the rupee appreciated by 14 paise to trade at 95 rupees and 82 paise against the US dollar.In the global crude oil market, Brent Crude was trading one per cent down at 105 US dollars and five cents per barrel, while WTI Crude was trading 1.7 per cent lower at 92 US dollars and 99 cents per barrel in intra-day trade.At the Multi Commodity Exchange, Gold for the October contract was trading 0.7 per cent up at 1,51,709 rupees per 10 grams, and Silver for the December contract was trading 1.3 per cent higher at 2,36,574 rupees per kilogram, when reports last came in.For more updates about the market activities, tune in to Akashvani’s bilingual programme ‘Market Mantra’ at 6:30 PM this evening.

. In Ladakh, RNU Akashvani Kargil has launched a special podcast series under the Seva Sankalp Abhiyan, with the first programme focusing on “Natural Farming – Towards Sustainable and Climate-Resilient Agriculture.”The programme featured Dr. Nazir Hussain, Scientist, Krishi Vigyan Kendra Kargil, in conversation with Anayat Ali of RNU Akashvani Kargil.During the podcast, Dr. Nazir Hussain explained the principles of natural farming and highlighted its role in improving soil health, reducing dependence on external chemical inputs and promoting sustainable and climate-resilient agriculture.He discussed various aspects of the National Mission on Natural Farming, including chemical-free cultivation, livestock integration, diversified cropping, use of locally available bio-inputs and integration of traditional agricultural knowledge with scientific practices.Dr. Hussain said natural farming has considerable potential in Ladakh and Kargil, where agriculture is characterised by a short growing season, cold climatic conditions and limited water availability. He stressed the need for locally adapted practices, scientific research, farmer training and awareness for its successful adoption in the region.Comparing natural farming with organic farming, Dr. Hussain said natural farming can be more effective and efficient in boosting production while reducing farmers’ dependence on externally purchased inputs.The discussion also covered crop productivity, input costs, farmers’ income, water management, climate resilience and the need to make the transition towards natural farming economically viable for farmers.The special podcast series, produced by RNU Akashvani Kargil under the Seva Sankalp Abhiyan, will be broadcast daily at 4:30 PM from Akashvani Kargil. The programmes will also be available on the AIRNews Kargil YouTube channel.

. In Men’s Cricket, Virat Kohli’s majestic century and Shubman Gill’s fluent hundred powered India to a commanding eight-wicket victory over West Indies in the first ODI in Thiruvananthapuram last night.Kohli remained unbeaten on a sensational 139, while Ruturaj Gaikwad finished unbeaten on 13. Chasing a target of 296, India made 300 for two in 41.4 overs to take a 1-0 lead in the three-match ODI series.Kohli’s innings was the centrepiece of India’s successful chase as the former India captain produced an aggressive display after initially settling into the innings. The century was Kohli’s 55th in ODI cricket. He also became the second batter after Sachin Tendulkar to complete 15,000 ODI runs, reaching the landmark during his innings.Captain Gill also played a major role in the chase, scoring 110. Earlier, West Indies posted 295 for seven in their stipulated 50 overs, with Justin Greaves top-scoring with 101, while John Campbell made 62.For India, Kuldeep Yadav claimed four wickets, while Prasidh Krishna bagged two wickets. Nitish Kumar Reddy took one wicket. Kuldeep Yadav was declared Player of the Match.

. Iran has filed a formal protest with the UN aviation watchdog, International Civil Aviation Organization (ICAO) against US restrictions on Iranian aviation, as Tehran seeks to restore suspended flight routes. Iranian Civil Aviation Organization chief Abuzar Shiroudi talking to country’s state media said the protest, submitted in coordination with Iran’s Foreign Ministry, includes documents detailing disruptions to flights caused by the restrictions. He said, Iran is using all available legal avenues to remove barriers and resume flight routes that had previously been in operation. Since direct flights to Europe were restricted, Iran has relied on connecting services through regional airports, including Istanbul, as an alternative for passengers.Iran has also filed a case at the International Court of Justice in The Hague, concerning attacks on airports, aircraft and radar systems. Shiroudi said the ICAO had ruled in Iran’s favour, while the ICJ case remains under review.The move follows US sanctions announced on 8th of this month against 36 targets linked to Iran’s aviation sector, including 27 Iranian airlines. Washington said the measures, which were part of “Operation Economic Outcast,” were aimed at disrupting what it described as Iran’s use of the aviation sector to transport weapons, personnel and illicit cargo.Iran said it is continuing diplomatic and legal efforts to restore flight connections and remove barriers affecting its aviation sector.

. At the Asian Games in Japan, India’s Ancy SojanEdappilly has wonthe silver medal in the women’s long jump at Aichi-Nagoya in Japan today. Sarvesh Kusharewon silvermedal in Men’s high jump.In Squash, the country clinched two silver medals with Abhay Singh winning silver in the Men’s Singles and Anahat Singh bagging a silver medal in Women’s Singles’ events.Tejaswin Shankar bagged a bronze medal in the decathlon. Harita Bhadra won the bronze in the women’s 200 metres event and Parul Chaudhary won bronze medal in women’s 3000m steeplechase event.President Droupadi Murmu extended wishes to all medal-winners.Currently, India is at 12th position in medal tally with a total of 37 medals, including four gold, 16sliverand 17 bronze medals.

. Prime Minister Narendra Modi congratulated javelin thrower Yashvir Singh on winning the Silver with a personal best and Rohit Yadav on bringing home the Bronze meda at the Asian Games. Sharing a thread on a social media platform, Mr Modi extended best wishes to Parul Chaudhary on winning bronze in the Women’s 5 thousand metres. He also conveyed best wishes to Gulveer Singh on winning the Silver in the Men’s 1500 metres. Mr Modi noted that Gulveer’s achievement becomes more special as it was a personal best. The Prime Minister also congratulated Vithya Ramraj on claiming the Bronze medal in the Women’s 4 hundred metres hurdles. He wished that Vithya keep scaling new heights of success in the times to come.Further, Mr Modi congratulated Murali Sreeshankar, saying that his leap earned him a place on the Men’s Long Jump podium. The Prime Minister extended his best wishes to all the athletes for their future.

. In Nepal, at least four people lost their lives and 12 others are missing after an avalanche struck the base camp of Mount Himlung in mountainous Manang district. According to Manang’s Chief District Officer Mukti Prasad Khanal, the bodies of four people have been recovered from the site. Two bodies have been airlifted to Kathmandu, while two others have been brought to Chame, the district headquarters. More than two dozen expedition guides and support staff from various expedition companies were believed to have been stationed at the base camp of the 7,126-meter-tall mountain when the avalanche struck the area. They had been preparing the site by fixing ropes and setting up tents ahead of the autumn climbing season.Officials said 11 people have made contact following the incident, while 27 people were believed to have been at the base camp when the avalanche hit. Rescue operations are underway with helicopters deployed to the affected area. Improved weather conditions have helped rescue efforts after several days of heavy rainfall triggered landslides and flooding in parts of Nepal, including Manang.The incident comes just a month after a catastrophic flooding disaster near the Nepal-China border, triggered by a huge glacier collapse and landslide, killed more than 1,400 people and left more than 5,000 missing.

. The Central Board of Direct Taxes (CBDT) extended the due date for filing income-tax returns for Assessment Year 2026-27 for taxpayers covered under audit provisions. The I-T return filing deadline has been extended from October 31 to November 21, 2026.The corresponding deadline for furnishing the tax audit report has also been extended from September 30 to October 21, 2026. The extension applies to specified taxpayers covered under Section 139 of the Income-tax Act, 1961. The CBDT said the extension will provide additional time to the specified taxpayers to complete their return filing. A formal order or notification giving effect to the decision will be issued separately.Under the revised timeline, applicable taxpayers will have to furnish their audit reports by October 21, followed by filing of their income-tax returns by November 21, 2026.

. The India Meteorological Department (IMD) has issued a red colour warning for heavy to very heavy rainfall with isolated extremely heavy rainfall over Uttar Pradesh and Uttarakhand tomorrow. According to IMD, heavy to very heavy rainfall is likely over Chhattisgarh and Madhya Pradesh tomorrow. The districts that are likely to receive heavy rainfall include Rampur, Pilibhit, Bareilly, Shahjahanpur and Bahraich. Meanwhile, districts of Madhya Pradesh which are expected to receive rainfall include Satna, Chhatarpur, Tikamgarh and Niwari.IMD said that the line of withdrawal of Southwest Monsoon continues to pass through Gurdaspur, Chandigarh, Muzaffarnagar, Aligarh, Dholpur, Udaipur, Deesa and Naliya.The Met Department has also predicted heavy rainfall over Delhi, Haryana, Chandigarh, Bihar, Himachal Pradesh, Jharkhand, Odisha, Sub-Himalayan West Bengal and Sikkim for the day. Thunderstorms accompanied by lightning and gusty windsare expectedto prevail over Punjab, Madhya Pradesh, Vidarbha, Andhra Pradesh, Kerala, Mahe, Telangana, Andaman and Nicobar Islands and parts of Northeast during the next two days.Meanwhile, parts of Delhi are expected to witness light to moderate rainfall tomorrow.

. Indian-origin chess prodigy Bodhana Sivanandan has created history by becoming the youngest Woman Grandmaster. The 11-year-old, who represents England, achieved the milestone at the 46th Chess Olympiad which concluded yesterday at Samarkand in Uzbekistan. Bodhana played all 11 rounds on England’s top board and finished the tournament with eight points.Her performance also earned her a second International Master (IM) norm, which takes her another step closer to becoming an international master. Bodhana first discovered chess during the COVID-19 lockdown and has since gone on to break several records. Last month, she became Britain’s youngest-ever Women’s Chess Champion at the 2026 British Chess Championships. The London schoolgirl says she wants to continue playing and making history in the game.

. Union Minister of State for Law and Justice Arjun Ram Meghwal today addressed the 15th United Nations Congress on Crime Prevention and Criminal Justice in Abu Dhabi, UAE. In his address, the Minister highlighted India’s efforts towards digital justice, stronger measures to combat cybercrime and terrorism, enhanced international cooperation and timely delivery of justice. The Union Minister also briefed the participating delegates on reforms undertaken through India’s new criminal laws and the country’s commitment to strengthening the criminal justice system in accordance with global standards.On the sidelines of the event, Shri. Meghwal also met UAE’s Minister of Justice Abdullah Sultan bin Awad Al Nuaimi. The two sides discussed ways to further strengthen legal cooperation between India and the UAE.The UN Congress on Crime Prevention and Criminal Justice also called the ‘UN Crime Congress’ is the world’s largest and most diverse gathering of policy-makers, practitioners, academia, intergovernmental organizations and civil society in the field of crime prevention and criminal justice. It is organised by the United Nations Office on Drugs and Crime (UNODC) – the UN agency mandated to assist Member States in combating illicit drugs, transnational organised crime, corruption and terrorism, while strengthening criminal justice and the rule of law. The 15th Crime Congress is being held in Abu Dhabi 26 September to 1 October 2026 under the overall theme “Accelerating crime prevention, criminal justice and the rule of law: protecting people and planet and achieving the 2030 Agenda for Sustainable Development in the digital age”.

. India Meteorological Department (IMD) has forecast heavy rainfall over Bihar, East Madhya Pradesh, East Uttar Pradesh, Uttarakhand, West Bengal and North Eastern parts of the country during the next two days. IMD said that thunderstorms accompanied by lightning and gusty winds are likely to prevail over Andhra Pradesh, Andaman and Nicobar Islands, Bihar, Jharkhand, Karnataka, Odisha, Sub-Himalayan West Bengal and Sikkim tomorrow. Meanwhile, Coastal Andhra Pradesh, Kerala and Mahe are expected to experience hot and humid weather till 8th of this month.

. Prime Minister Narendra Modi is completing 25 years in public service, a journey defined by the mantra of Jan Seva Se Desh Seva, and a relentless commitment that continues. Guided by this vision for Seva and Sushasan, the Government has been ceaselessly working towards achieving the goal of a Viksit Bharat by 2047. Through inclusive development and social empowerment, this dedication is transforming lives. Today, in our special series, we bring you an instance of how this vision has been translated into creation of the post of Chief of Defence Staff.Earlier, India’s three armed services – Army, Navy and the Air Force – planned, trained, procured and advised the government separately. Proposals for greater jointness had been made repeatedly since the Kargil Review Committee of 1999 and the Group of Ministers that followed it, but no single officer held authority across all three services. On the 15th of August 2019, Prime Minister Narendra Modi, in his Independence Day address, announced the creation of the post of Chief of Defence Staff from the ramparts of the Red Fort. Prime Minister Modi said this will lead to better coordination among the three services.The Cabinet approved the decision in December 2019, along with a new Department of Military Affairs within the Ministry of Defence for the CDS to head.  Talking to Akashvani News, retired Lt General Sanjay Kulkarni said the appointment of CDS made it possible for the government to have one point of contact for advice on allmiltarymatters.After the formation of the post of CDS, all three forces have now got effective leadership at the top level.

. Prime Minister Narendra Modi has congratulated Abhay Singh and Anahat Singh on winning the silver medal in Men’s Singles Squash and Women’s Singles Squash at the Asian Games 2026. In a social media post, Mr Modi said that this achievement reflects Abhay Singh’s years of hard work, skill, and determination. He also commended Anahat Singh for showing tremendous skill while competing against some of the finest players.The Prime Minister also congratulated Ancy Sojan on winning the silver medal in the Women’s Long Jump. He said that her strong and spirited performance has brought immense joy to the nation. Mr Modi also extended his greetings to Harita Bhadra for winning the Bronze Medal in the Women’s 200 Metres event at the Asian Games 2026. He said that this is Harita Bhadra’s Asian Games debut, and she raced with confidence and determination to secure a place on the podium.

. A 60-member Indian Armed Forces contingent departed for Oskemen in Kazakhstan to participate in the ninth edition of the India-Kazakhstan Joint Military Exercise KAZIND-2026.The Defence Ministry said that the exercise aims to enhance interoperability and strengthen the joint capability of both forces to undertake joint counter-terrorism operations in a sub-conventional environment under a United Nations mandate. It added that the exercise will provide an opportunity for both sides to benefit from each other’s operational experience while strengthening professional bonds, mutual trust and camaraderie.The participating contingents will train together in joint responses to terrorist actions, raids, search-and-destroy missions and Special Heliborne Operations, among other activities. The Indian contingent is drawn mainly from a battalion of the Garhwal Rifles, along with troops from other arms and services and personnel from the Indian Air Force.The exercise is scheduled to continue until the 11th of next month. The Ministry also said that the exercise will further deepen military-to-military cooperation between India and Kazakhstan. It added that the exercise will reinforce the shared commitment of both nations towards regional peace, stability and collective security.

. Foreign Portfolio Investors (FPIs) have offloaded Indian equities worth 17,131 crore rupees in September so far. According to the latest depository data, out of the total net outflows, 25,682 crore rupees were withdrawn through sales on stock exchanges, as geopolitical uncertainty, elevated US bond yields, and crude oil prices weighed on investors’ risk appetite. However, the trend of FPI investment through the primary market has continued this month, with FPIs infusing 8,551 crore rupees in the primary market in September so far.Meanwhile, Foreign investors also extended their selling to the debt market during the period under review. In September so far, outflows from the debt securities through the Fully Accessible Route (FAR) stood at 7,385 crore rupees. FPIs have withdrawn 3,021 crore rupees through the Voluntary Retention Route (VRR) and 1,889 crore rupees through the General Limit route.

. Benchmark domestic equity indices slumped over 1.6 percent today. The Sensex tanked 1, 248 points to close at 73, 581 while the Nifty plunged 384 points to settle at 23,063.In the broader market at the National Stock Exchange, the Midcap 100 index shed 2.3 per cent, while the Smallcap 100 index lost over 1.5%.This morning, Markets opened with a gap-down as spike in bond yields, elevated crude oil prices and a sell-off in banking and insurance stocks weighed on the indices. The Sensex and Nifty remained under pressure throughout the session, with sell-off intensifying during the second half of the trade.In the Sensex pack, 29 out of 30 companies logged losses with NTPC remaining unchanged. Among the top under performers, Bajaj Finance lost 5.5%, Axis Bank declined 4.7 per cent and Bajaj Finserv fell 4.1 per cent.In the sectoral indices on the BSE, all 28 sectors edged downward. Among the top losers, Mid-Small Private Banks declined 2.8 per cent, Housing Finance lost 2.6 per cent and Financial Services shed more than 2.3 per cent.The overall market breadth at the BSE was negative, as shares of 2,884 companies declined, 1,473 advanced and 216 remained unchanged.

. Today is World Heart Day. The day is observed every year on 29th of September to raise public awareness about cardiovascular diseases, their prevention and their global impact.In a social media post, Union Health and Family Welfare Minister JP Nadda has said that the day reminds people to recognise warning signs, adopt healthy lifestyle practices, manage risk factors and seek timely care. The Minister also renewed his commitment to protecting heart health and preventing cardiovascular diseases. He informed that the theme this year is Don’t Miss a Beat.

. In Nepal, 21 people have been killed, five remain missing and five others have been injured following four days of torrential rainfall, flooding and landslides.According to the National Disaster Risk Reduction and Management Authority, or NDRRMA, landslides accounted for the majority of the casualties, claiming 14 lives and leaving five people missing. Floods caused four deaths, while three fatalities were attributed to continuous heavy rainfall. The severe weather has directly affected 247 families across the country, completely destroying 260 homes and partially damaging another 80.The situation followed a low-pressure system originating in the Bay of Bengal, which brought heavy to excessive rainfall to several parts of Nepal from September 24 to 27.In response to rising water levels and landslides, emergency teams have relocated around 3,000 residents from high-risk areas to safer locations. In the worst-affected mountain districts of Jajarkot, Myagdi and Sankhuwasabha, people who were trapped have been evacuated by emergency helicopters. The disaster authority estimated that around 9,000 foreign tourists and trekkers were in Nepal during the period of heavy rainfall.This morning, authorities issued a warning for residents living along the Narayani River in central Nepal after the river crossed the nine-metre warning level and entered settlements. Highways leading to Chitwan, a major junction for travel across the country, also remain blocked due to landslides at several locations.Meanwhile, a landslide in neighbouring Baglung district has claimed four more lives. In another disaster, two bodies have been recovered following an avalanche near the base camp of Mount Himlung Himal in Nepal’s high-altitude Manang district.

. In Dubai, the Indian Consulate is organising a series of programmes as part of Seva Pakhwada to promote the spirit of service, community participation and national commitment.On Sunday, the Indian community came together in great strength for the Viksit Bharat Run 2026. The fitness run was organised near the iconic Dubai Frame by the Consulate General of India, in association with the Indian People’s Forum (IPF).  Consul General Dr. E. Vishnu Vardhan Reddy flagged off the run, which saw an enthusiastic response with around 3,000 registrations. The event represented a collective commitment towards the vision of a Viksit Bharat.The Consulate also organised a labour camp for Indian workers in Dubai, focusing on financial and medical literacy, and informed them about the Consulate services and helpline numbers.Earlier, the officials of the Indian Consulate also visited the Guru Nanak Darbar Gurudwara in the City, where they participated in Langar Seva as part of the observances.The activities are part of the ongoing Seva Pakhwada observances, underscoring the spirit of service and community engagement among members of the Indian diaspora in Dubai.

. Science and Technology Minister Dr Jitendra Singh has said that critical minerals are key to India’s energy security, industrial competitiveness and national security. The Minister said this while addressing a special plenary of the 3rd Global Summit on Advanced Materials, Critical Minerals, and Metals in New Delhi. Dr Singh said that critical minerals and metals will be a driving component of the next phase of technological development, with their importance extending beyond mining to energy security, industrial competitiveness and national security. He said that the global economy is undergoing a paradigm shift, with clean energy, electric mobility, semiconductors, telecommunications, aerospace, defence and nuclear energy emerging as major drivers of technological and industrial transformation. He added, India is now participating in this global discourse with much greater confidence and is preparing to assume a larger global role.Dr. Singh has called for early industry linkage with research and innovation, saying potential industry partners should be brought on board right from the beginning. He further said that a healthy synergy among research, industry, government and the non-government sector is essential for sustaining startups and entrepreneurs. The Minister also highlighted on building domestic capabilities for energy security as the world moves towards cleaner and greener sources of energy. He said that India’s next phase of growth in strategic technologies and materials will depend on working together of all stakeholders.

. The Government has said that the country’s National Highway network has grown by nearly 61 percent, to over one lakh 46 thousand kilometers in March this year from over 91 thousand kilometre in 2014. This rapid development has strengthened connectivity, improved access to markets and supported faster movement of people and goods.The greening of India’s National Highway network is guided by the Green Highways (Plantation, Transplantation, Beautification and Maintenance) Policy, 2015. The Policy was formulated to evolve a framework for plantations along National Highways and reduce the impact of air pollution and dust, meanwhile creating employment opportunities for local people.

. The Indian Meteorological Department (IMD) hasissued redalert for extremely heavy rainfall over isolated places of Chhattisgarh, Coastal Andhra Pradesh, Odisha and Telangana for the next two days. The Met Department has predicted heavy rainfall over Arunachal Pradesh, Assam, Meghalaya, Bihar, Jharkhand, Kerala, Maharashtra, West Bengal and Sikkim tomorrow. The weather department also forecast thunderstorms accompanied with highly gusty winds over Madhya Pradesh and Parts of North-East tomorrow.For Delhi, IMD said the national capital will witness mostly clear skies with no rain. The maximum temperature in Delhi is expected to be around 34 to 35 degrees Celsius, while the minimum temperature of 23 to 25 degrees Celsius.

. The US will not charge any tariff on certain speciality drugs and associated ingredients used for the treatment of rare medical conditions imported from India and 19 other countries.The US Commerce Department published the list of countries in the Federal Register as it prepares to impose a 100 per cent tariff on certain patented pharmaceutical imports and their associated ingredients from September 29.On April 2, President Donald Trump issued a proclamation to impose tariffs on imports of patented pharmaceuticals, biologics, and associated ingredients into the US as part of efforts to encourage domestic production.Eligible products for the zero per cent tariff rate include all drugs designated for rare diseases, infertility treatments, cell therapies, gene therapies, antibody-drug conjugates (ADCs), and animal pharmaceuticals. Components of these drugs are also subject to a zero per cent tariff rate.Besides India, the other countries in the zero tariff rate category are Argentina, Bangladesh, Cambodia, Ecuador, El Salvador, the European Union, Guatemala, Indonesia, Japan, Jordan, Malaysia, North Macedonia, South Korea, Switzerland, Liechtenstein, Taiwan, Thailand, Britain and Vietnam.The notice said qualifying products from these jurisdictions could receive a zero per cent tariff because they have a current or forthcoming trade and security framework agreement with the US.The exemptions are part of the implementation of Trump’s April proclamation adjusting imports of pharmaceuticals and pharmaceutical ingredients under Section 232 of the Trade Expansion Act.

. The Agricultural and Processed Food Products Export Development Authority (APEDA) facilitated the flag-off of a one MT consignment of GI-tagged Gulbarga Tur Dal from Karnataka to the Maldives. The consignment, exported yesterday by M/s Silken Global Exports and Imports, Mysuru, through its Farmer Producer Organisation (FPO)-led brand, will be transported to the Maldives by sea. The Ministry of Commerce and Industry said that the initiative is aimed at expanding international markets for India’s GI-tagged agricultural products and strengthening the participation of FPO-led brands in agri exports.It added that a key feature of the export-linked value chain is improved price realisation for farmers, which enables farmers to realise 82 rupees per kg against prevailing market price of 60 rupees per kg. It provides FPOs an opportunity to participate more closely in export-oriented value chains and connect producers with international markets. The Ministry further noted that the export is expected to pave the way for regular shipments of Gulbarga Tur Dal to the Maldives, creating sustained market opportunities for producers and exporters from Karnataka. The initiative is also expected to support greater value realisation for farmers and enable FPOs and farmers to integrate more closely with export-oriented value chains.

. India’s industrial output, as measured by the Index of Industrial Production (IIP), grew by 8% year-on-year in August this year. The latest data indicate that industrial activity continued to expand at a healthy pace, with the upward revision in July’s IIP growth to 7.4% from the earlier estimate of 6.7%.According to government data released today, electricity and gas supply recorded strong growth of 12.3% in August, while manufacturing, which carries the heaviest weight in the index, expanded by 9%. Water supply, sewerage and waste management also registered healthy growth of 6.3%. However, the mining sector remained a laggard, contracting by 5.6% during the period under review.

. Chief Economic Adviser V. Anantha Nageswaran has highlighted India’s ability to attract foreign capital with its broader manufacturing and overall reforms. Addressing the 13th PAFI annual forum in New Delhi, Mr Nageswaran emphasized that the most important thing for the industry is global competitiveness. He added that the global environment in which investment decisions are made has now shifted, making it important to assess India’s foreign direct investment performance in that context.Mr Nageswaran also pointed to investor protection, tax-policy certainty and consistency, and availability of skilled talent and logistics as other factors that can influence investment decisions. He noted that changing global interest-rate environments could also have a significant bearing on the cost of capital and cross-border investment flows.

. India has secured the 10th position at the 48th WorldSkills Competition in Shanghai, China. India won six Silver Medals and 20 Medals for Excellence at the competition. The Ministry of Skill Development and Entrepreneurship informed that India won six Silver Medals and 20 Medals for Excellence at the competition.Congratulating Team India on its performance, Minister of State for Skill Development and Entrepreneurship, Jayant Chaudhary said, the Team India’s remarkable performance at the event marks a significant leap in our global skills journey. He said that, surpassing previous performance, the country’s young competitors have demonstrated the growing strength and competitiveness of India’s skilled talent.WorldSkills is the world’s leading international skills competition, bringing together young professionals from participating countries and regions to demonstrate excellence across a wide range of vocational and technical skills.

. Union Finance Minister Nirmala Sitharaman has reached Doha in Qatar to participate in the 11th Annual Meeting of the Asian Infrastructure Investment Bank (AIIB) and the AIIB Investors Dialogue 2026.The Annual Meeting will bring together member delegations, policymakers and other stakeholders from around the world to discuss the AIIB’s strategic direction, operational priorities and future agenda.

. In the Asian Games 2026 in Japan, India’s Esha Singh won the silver medal in the women’s 25-metre pistol individual competition at Aichi-Nagoya today. The 21-year-old shooter won the medal with 38 points to finish second.Indian athlete Pincky Balhara secured the bronze medal in the women’s under-78kg Kurash event at Aichi-Nagoya today. She won the medal after defeating South Korea’s Lim Garam 3-0 in the quarter-finals.Earlier, the Indian men’s cricket team entered the semi-finals without taking the field after its quarter-final against Afghanistan was abandoned due to inclement weather at Aichi-Nagoya in Japan today. The defending champion side made it to the last four as it is ranked number one in the ICC T20I rankings, while Afghanistan is currently placed 10th. India will take on the winner of the quarter-final between Nepal and Sri Lanka in the semi-final.In the women’s boxing event, Indian Olympic medallist Lovlina Borgohain secured a medal in the 75-kilogram category with a 5-0 quarter-final win over South Korea’s Seong Suyeon.India are currently placed 12th in the medal standings, with an overall tally of 39 medals, including four gold, 17 silver and 18 bronze.President Droupadi Murmu has congratulated Esha Singh on winning the silver medal in the women’s 25m pistol event at the Asian Games 2026. In a social media post, President Murmu said that her exceptional performance reflected great skill, precision and consistency. The President added that this medal is a proud addition to her sporting journey.

The second edition of the India Art, Architecture and Design Biennale (IAADB) will be held from 4th December 2026 to 21st March 2027 in New Delhi.The theme of this 108-day Biennale is ‘Tat Tvam Asi – Reconnecting in an Age of Distraction’. Talking exclusively to Akashvani News, Secretary of the Ministry of Culture, Vivek Aggarwal said that, the Biennale will feature art installations at iconic heritage sites of the National Capital, including Purana Qila, Red Fort, Safdarjung Tomb, Qutub Minar, Qila Rai Pithora and Lodhi Garden. He said that the theme of this year’s Biennale directly takes inspiration from India’s ancient traditions and spiritual thought, which emphasize self-introspection and the unity of the individual with the larger universal consciousness.Mr Aggarwal said that the Ministry aims to take IAADB to a global level by encouraging participation from international pavilions and artists, Indian states and the private sector.Speaking about the cultural diplomacy of India, He said that cultural exchange is an important component of cultural diplomacy and the country’s soft power. Mr Aggarwal added that participation of foreign countries will provide an opportunity for Indian and international audiences to experience diverse art forms and will help position the Biennale on the global cultural calendar.Underlining the importance of Art and Design students in this Biennale, He said that the Ministry plans to involve students, particularly those pursuing art and design, in various activities associated with the Biennale, providing them opportunities to engage with artists and the wider creative ecosystem.The second edition of the India Art, Architecture & Design Biennale 2026 is the largest platform which offers artists, curators, galleries, corporates, architects, designers, cultural institutions and other stakeholders a chance to connect with culture and the creative world. This edition is conceived not as a single exhibition in a single location but as a city-wide cultural platform. Visitors will have an opportunity to experience the historical monuments along with contemporary art installations.

The Supreme Court will tomorrow hear a plea challenging the Centre’s decision to impose a Merchant Discount Rate (MDR) on specified UPI person-to-merchant transactions of over 2,000 rupees.Ending nearly six years of fully free UPI payments, the government has introduced a 0.4 per cent fee on transfers of over 2,000 Rs made to merchants through the UPI platform from October 15, while explicitly ring-fencing everyday person-to-person transactions and small payments from any charge. The MDR will be capped at 300 Rs for payments of 75,000 Rs and above.Essential and thin-margin sectors — railways, telecom, insurance, fuel and agricultural inputs — will pay a flat MDR of 5 Rs per transaction above 2,000 Rs.Payments into mutual funds, securities and through stockbrokers and dealers will attract 0.02 per cent MDR, also capped at 300 Rs. Bench of Chief Justice of India Justice Surya Kant and Justices Joymalya Bagchi and V Mohana will hear the plea.The Public Interest Litigation (PIL) filed by advocate Anjan Datta has challenged the Centre’s decision. The plea alleged that the levy has been introduced without adequate statutory safeguards, transparency or public consultation.

The Supreme Court has directed the Centre and the Central Board of Secondary Education (CBSE) to consider extending to the current Class 6 students the exemption from the three-language framework that has been granted to students of Class 7.A bench comprising Chief Justice Surya Kant and Justices Joymalya Bagchi and V Mohana asked Solicitor General Tushar Mehta and Additional Solicitor General Aishwarya Bhati, appearing for the Centre and the CBSE, to grant the same relaxation granted to students of Classes 7, 8 and 9 to students of Class 6 this year.On September 17, the top court had asked the CBSE to consider implementing its policy mandating the study of three languages, including two native Indian languages, for Class 6 students from the next academic session starting in 2027.According to CBSE’s statement, the current batches studying in Classes 7, 8 and 9 would not be required to give board examination in third language when they progress to Class 10.The Solicitor General has submitted that about 99 per cent of schools have adopted the third-language policy and have been provided the necessary facilities, and only about 1.2 per cent of the schools have not.During the hearing, the Centre, however, maintained that it was not inclined to exempt the current Class 6 batch from the policy and said students should pursue the new language framework from the current academic year itself.The Solicitor General told the bench that the latest data showed that implementation-related difficulties affected only about 1.2 per cent of CBSE-affiliated schools.According to the Centre, nearly 99 per cent of schools had adopted the third-language policy and had the necessary facilities.Justice Bagchi suggested that the implementation for students who are already in Class 6 could be deferred, allowing the CBSE additional time to put the required infrastructure in place.The dispute relates to the CBSE’s decision to align its scheme of studies with the National Education Policy, 2020 and the National Curriculum Framework for School Education, 2023. Under the framework, students are required to study three languages, with at least two being categorised as Indian.

The Ministry of Education, in coordination with the External Affairs Ministry is organizing a two day Bharat Innovates Exposition from today at Bharat Mandapam in New Delhi to showcase India’s Deep-Tech innovations as a lead up to and alongside the 18th BRICS Summit 2026. The Exposition is showcasing 37 India’s Deep-Tech startups and ventures alligning with the theme of India’s BRICS Chairship Building for Resilience, Innovation, Cooperation and Sustainability. The event is providing participating innovators an opportunity to network with CEOs, investors, business leaders and industry representatives from BRICS member countries. Ministry of Eduaction said that the event will facilitate opportunities for Business to Business engagements, technology partnerships, investment discussions, business linkages and international market access.

. India continued its impressive medal-winning run at the Asian Games in Aichi-Nagoya, Japan, today, with athletes making their mark across shooting, cricket, kurash and boxing. The country added eight more medals to its tally so far today, while the Indian men’s cricket team also advanced to the semi-finals. In athletics, India secured a double podium finish in the men’s javelin throw, with Yashvir Singh clinching silver and Rohit Yadav bagging the bronze medal. Commonwealth Games bronze medallist Yashvir Singh delivered a personal best of 85.72 metres to secure the silver medal. Sri Lanka’s Rumesh Pathirage took gold with a throw of 88.55 metres. India’s Rohit Yadav completed the podium with an effort of 84.35 metres, giving India a double podium finish in the event.India’s Sreeshankar Murali clinched the silver medal in the men’s long jump, recording a best effort of 8.07 metres. The two-time Commonwealth Games silver medallist successfully defended the silver medal he won at the previous Asian Games. However, Sreeshankar’s competition ended prematurely after he suffered an injury during his fourth attempt. He subsequently retired from the event.Athlete Gulveer Singh has won his second silver medal at the ongoing Games, finishing runner-up in the men’s 1,500-metre event. Gulveer clocked a personal best of 3 minutes 37-point-92 seconds to claim the silver medal. The athlete had earlier won silver in the men’s 10,000 metres event.In shooting, Esha Singh has won the silver medal in the women’s 25-metre pistol individual event. The 21-year-old Indian shooter finished second with a score of 38 points.Parul Chaudhary has won her second bronze medal at the Games, adding another podium finish in athletics. Chaudhary clocked 15 minutes 14-point-61 seconds to finish third in the women’s 5,000-metre event. She had earlier won bronze in the women’s 3,000-metre steeplechase. The two medals have come within three days, as Chaudhary continues her impressive campaign at the Games.Athlete Vithya Ramraj has won the bronze medal in the women’s 400-metre hurdles, setting a new national record in the process. Ramraj clocked a personal best of 54-point-75 seconds to finish third and broke a more than four-decade-old national record created by the legendary P T Usha.India also secured a bronze medal in Kurash, with Pincky Balhara finishing third in the women’s under-78-kilogram category. Balhara defeated South Korea’s Lim Garam 3-nil in the quarterfinals to secure her place on the podium.In boxing, India has assured itself of three more medals, with Lovlina Borgohain, Priya Ghanghas and Kapil Pokhariya advancing to the semi-finals in their respective weight categories. Olympic medallist Lovlina defeated South Korea’s Seong Suyeon by a unanimous 5-nil verdict in the quarterfinals of the 75-kilogram category. Priya also booked her place in the semi-finals of the women’s 60-kilogram category. She defeated Tajikistan’s Mijgona Samadova 5-nil in the quarterfinals.Kapil Pokhariya moved to the last four with 5-0 win over South Korea’s Kim Gichae in Men’s 90kg category.Meanwhile, the Indian men’s cricket team has advanced to the semi-finals without taking the field. Its quarterfinal against Afghanistan was abandoned due to inclement weather in Aichi-Nagoya. As the defending champions, India progressed on the basis of its higher position in the ICC T20 International rankings. India are ranked number one, while Afghanistan are currently tenth. India will face the winner of the quarterfinal between Nepal and Sri Lanka in the semi-final.The Indian Men’s Hockey team has secured its place in the semi-finals after registering a thumping 10-nil victory over Bangladesh in its final pool match. India will face arch-rivals Pakistan on the 1st of October.India’s 4×100-metre relay team qualified for the final today. The Indian quartet of Gurindervir Singh, Abinaya Rajarajan, Animesh Kujur and Haritha Bhadra clocked 41-point-54 seconds to finish second in their heat and third overall. With the performance, the Indian team secured its place in the final, which will be held tomorrow.In Squash, the Indian women’s and men’s teams marched into the quarterfinals. Indian women, seeded third, got past Japan, while the men’s team defeated South Korea to seal a place in the last eight stage.India are currently 12th in the Asian Games medal standings, with a total of 45 medals comprising four gold, 20 silver and 21 bronze.

. Today is World Suicide Prevention Day. The day is observed worldwide to raise awareness about suicide prevention and the importance of mental health.The occasion reminds us that people facing emotional distress or difficult circumstances need timely support, understanding and appropriate care. Experts emphasise that listening to someone with patience and without judgement can encourage them to seek help and support.On this Day, people are encouraged to remain attentive to the emotional well-being of those around them and, when required, guide them towards family members, trusted persons or mental health professionals.

. The FASTag Annual Pass has crossed the significant milestone of one crore passes issued after its launch on 15th August last year. The Ministry of Road Transport and Highways said that the milestone reflects growing acceptance of the Annual Pass among private vehicle owners for providing a seamless and economical travel option on the National Highways and Expressways.It said that the pass is applicable on about more than one thousand fee plazas on National Highways and National Expressways which eliminates the need to frequently recharge FASTag through one-time fee payment of three thousand seventy five rupees for one year validity or 200 toll plaza crossings.

. The India Meteorological Department (IMD) has forecast heavy rainfall over Andaman and Nicobar Islands, South Interior Karnataka and Uttarakhand tomorrow. It has also predicted thunderstorms accompanied with lightning and gusty winds over North Eastern parts of India, including Assam, Meghalaya, Nagaland, Manipur, Mizoram and Tripura, during the next two days. According to IMD, Himachal Pradesh, Rajasthan, Tamil Nadu, Puducherry, Karaikal, Andhra Pradesh, Bihar, Madhya Maharashtra, Marathwada, Odisha and Telangana are also likely to witness similar weather conditions tomorrow.

. Benchmark domestic equity indices declined sharply by over 1.5% today. The Sensex plunged 1,240 points to close at 72,772. The Nifty shed 360 points to settle at 22 thousand 780. In the broader market at the National Stock Exchange, the Midcap 100 index tumbled 1.6%, while the Smallcap 100 index tanked 1.8%.In the Sensex pack, 29 of the 30 constituent companies logged losses, with Infosys emerging as the lone gainer, rising 0.2%. Among the top underperformers, Larsen and Toubro slumped 2.8%, PowerGrid declined 2.6%, and Adani Ports fell 2.4%.In the sectoral indices on the BSE, all 28 sectors edged lower. Among the top laggards,PSU Banks skidded 3.2%, Power, Telecommunication, and Utilities lost 2.3% each and Mid-Small Private Banks dropped 2.2%.The overall market breadth at the BSE was negative, as shares of 3218 companies declined, 1271 advanced and 228 remained unchanged.

National Payments Corporation of India (NPCI) Managing Director and CEO Dilip Asbe today said around 75 per cent of transaction volumes would fall outside the scope of the new merchant discount rate (MDR) regime, as 96 per cent of transactions are below 2,000 rupees.Addressing the SBI Banking and Economics Conclave in Mumbai, Asbe said there is “huge miscommunication and misinformation” surrounding the MDR regime and that NPCI and the government is trying to provide clear information.Mr Asbe clarified that the new regime will not hurt UPI volumes because most of the MDR will come from merchants who already accept credit cards and therefore, already pay MDR.

India defended the prestigious Nona Gaprindashvili Trophy at the 46th Chess Olympiad in Samarkand, Uzbekistan, finishing as the best overall nation after picking up a silver in the Open section and a bronze in the Women’s event.The Indian men played out a draw with Hungary and settled for the silver medal on a tie-break, while the women drew with Georgia to bring home the bronze in the Chess Olympiad that concluded today.This marks the third straight edition where India have won the trophy, having claimed it on home turf in 2022, during their historic double-gold campaign in Budapest in 2024, including the latest in Samarkand.The Uzbekistan team regained the gold medal in the open section after winning the final round game against Ukraine by a 2,5-1.5 points. The Uzbeks ended with 20 points out of a possible 22, winning as many as 10 rounds and losing a lone match against Germany.The Indian men ended up with 18 points and were tied for the second spot with Germany that defeated Holland. However, thanks to a better tie-break score, the Indian team ended with silver, while Germany had to be content with the bronze.In the women’s section, China annexed the gold with another fine performance against Vietnam, winning by a 3-1 margin. The Chinese team also ended with 20 points in all, a couple of points more than second-placed Kazakhstan.

. In the Women’s Trap Team event at the Asian Games 2026, Indian shooters Neeru Dhanda, Aashima Ahlawat and Manisha Keer have won a silver medal. The Indian trio finished with a combined score of 328 points to secure the silver, finishing three points ahead of Kuwait, who took bronze with 325.China won the gold medal with a score of 346. Neeru Dhanda was India’s top performer with a score of 118 out of 125, while Aashima and Manisha contributed 106 and 104, respectively. Neeru also finished joint-top in the individual qualifying round alongside Qatar’s Ray Bassil and will compete in the individual final later today.In athletics, India secured a double podium finish in the men’s javelin throw. Yashvir Singh won the silver medal with a personal-best effort of 85.72 metres, while Rohit Yadav claimed bronze with a throw of 84.35 metres.In the men’s long jump, Sreeshankar Murali secured the silver medal with a best effort of 8.07 metres. Gulveer Singh also added another silver to his tally after finishing runner-up in the men’s 1,500 metres. He had earlier won silver in the men’s 10,000 metres.In shooting, Esha Singh won silver in the women’s 25-metre pistol individual event. The 21-year-old Indian shooter finished second with a score of 38 points.Parul Chaudhary secured her second bronze medal of the Games in the women’s 5,000 metres, having earlier finished third in the women’s 3,000-metre steeplechase.The silver added to India’s medal tally at the ongoing Asian Games, with the country currently placed 12th with 46 medals, including four gold, 21 silver and 21 bronze.President Droupadi Murmu has congratulated Neeru Dhanda, Aashima Ahlawat and Manisha Keer on winning the Silver Medal in the Women’s Trap Team event at the Asian Games 2026. In a social media post, the President said that their precision and steady focus have brought this success. President Murmu has wished them to continue to keep their sights set on many more memorable achievements.
